CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 1 (Purpose)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The purpose of this Act is to provide for matters concerning higher education pursuant to 
Article 9 of the Framework Act on Education
.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 2 (Types of schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The following schools shall be established to provide higher education:
1.
 Universities and colleges;
2.
 Industrial colleges;
3.
 Teachers' colleges;
4.
 Junior colleges;
5.
 Air colleges, correspondence colleges, air and correspondence colleges and cyber colleges (hereinafter referred to as "cyber colleges");
6.
 Technical colleges;
7.
 Various kinds of schools.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 3 (Classification of national schools, public schools, and private schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Schools listed in the subparagraphs of 
Article 2
 (hereinafter referred to as "schools") shall be classified into national schools established and managed by the State, or established by the State as national university corporations, public schools (they may be classified into city schools and 
Do
 schools according to the founding entities) established and managed by local governments and private schools established and managed by incorporated school foundations.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 4 (Establishment of schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Any person who intends to establish a school shall meet the conditions for establishing facilities, equipment, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2)
 Establishment of a school by any party other than the State requires authorization from the Minister of Education. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(3)
 Where any founder or manager of a public or private school intends to abolish the school or modify important matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, he or she shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Education. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 5 (Guidance and supervision)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Schools shall be under the guidance and supervision of the Minister of Education. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(2)
 If the Minister of Education deems it necessary to guide and supervise schools, he or she may request the heads of schools to submit relevant data, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 6 (School regulations)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The head of a school (where a person establishes a school, the person who intends to establish the school) may establish or amend school regulations (hereinafter referred to as "school regulations") within the scope of statutes or regulations.
(2)
 Necessary matters such as the entries in and procedures for the formulation and amendments of school regulations, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 7 (Educational finances)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The State and local governments may provide schools with financial support or subsidies to help them cover the financial resources required for managing quality of education in response to rapid changes in the educational environment, such as disasters. <Amended on Oct. 20, 2020>
(2)
 Schools shall disclose their budgets and account settlements, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(3)
 Deleted. <Sep. 24, 2021>
(4)
 Deleted. <Sep. 24, 2021>
(5)
 Deleted. <Sep. 24, 2021>
(6)
 Deleted. <Sep. 24, 2021>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 7-2 (Plan for, consultation on, and coordination of financial support)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Minister of Education shall formulate a master plan for financial support for higher education every five years in consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments to expand support for higher education and to invest its funds in a strategic way, and shall formulate an annual support plan detailing the direction of, and standards for investment in financial support, reflecting the master plan, and submit such support plan to the National Assembly after reporting it to the State Council.
(2)
 A master plan for financial support shall include the following matters: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2023>
1.
 The objectives of mid- and long-term investment in financial support for higher education, and the direction thereof;
2.
 Changes in the higher education environment and the financial outlook for colleges;
3.
 Direction for allocating financial support in accordance with the roles and characteristics of schools;
4.
 Major tasks and methods for implementation thereof;
5.
 Analysis of the performance of projects for financial support for higher education and a performance management plan;
6.
 Direction-setting for distribution of financial support for balanced regional development.
(3)
 Where the head of a central administrative agency intends to develop or change a project to provide funds or grant subsidies to schools, he or she shall consult with the Minister of Education on whether such project conforms to the master plan and support plan under paragraph (1), the direction of mid-and long-term policies on higher education, possible effects on schools, etc. In such cases, the head of the central administrative agency shall hear the opinions of the heads of local governments under 
Article 2 (1) 1 of the Local Autonomy Act
 in advance. <Amended on Jan. 21, 2025>
(4)
 The Minister of Education may request relevant institutions to submit data and conduct fact-finding surveys to investigate and analyze projects that provide funds or grant subsidies to schools and the outcomes thereof, and may notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies of the findings of the analysis and recommend that they reflect such findings in implementing relevant policies.
(5)
 The Minister of Education may operate a committee in which relevant institutions, experts, etc. participate, to deliberate on and coordinate matters relating to the formulation of a master plan and support plan under paragraph (1) and the consultation on, and coordination of, projects for financial support for higher education under paragraph (3).
(6)
 Matters necessary for the formulation of a master plan and support plan under paragraph (1); the consultation on, and coordination of, projects for financial support for high education under paragraph (3); the investigation and analysis of the projects for financial support and their outcomes under paragraph (4); and the organization and operation of the committee under paragraph (5) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[This Article added on Sep. 24, 2021

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 8 (Payment of experiment and practice expenses)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The State shall take such necessary measures as payment of experiment and practice expenses, research aid expenses and scholarships to encourage scholarship or academic research and educational research.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 8-2 (Health management of students and support for school meals)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The State and local governments may take necessary measures, such as securing human resources and budget, for the health care of students and support for school meals.
[This Article added on Oct. 22, 2024]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 9 (Support for mutual cooperation among schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The State and a local government shall provide support for facilitating the interchange of school teachers and research cooperation among schools.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 10 (School consultative body)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Universities, colleges, industrial colleges, teachers' colleges, junior colleges, cyber colleges, etc. may operate school consultative bodies comprised of representatives from respective schools for the development of higher education.
(2)
 The organization and operation of consultative bodies referred to in paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by other Acts.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 11 (Enrollment fees and enrollment fee deliberation committee)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Any founder or manager of a school may accept the payment of tuition fees and other charges (hereinafter referred to as "enrollment fees") made by settlements in cash or by credit card, debit card, or prepaid card referred to in 
Article 2 of the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act
. In such cases, a student may pay tuition and fees payable for the relevant semester in two or more installments, as prescribed by school regulations. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2016; Dec. 3, 2019>
(2)
 Notwithstanding paragraph (1), no founder or manager of a school (excluding any graduate school university referred to in 
Article 30)
 shall receive admission fees from persons who enter or transfer to the relevant school (excluding persons who enter or transfer to a degree course or research course established in a graduate school pursuant to 
Article 29
 or a degree course integrated under 
Article 29-3)
. <Added on Dec. 3, 2019>
(3)
 Each school shall establish and operate an enrollment fee deliberation committee comprised of faculties (in cases of a private university, including its foundation members recommended by the school foundation), students, related experts, etc. to set enrollment fees. In such cases, the student members shall account for at least 3/10 of the quorum of the committee, with members of each unit accounting for less than 5/10 of the quorum; and the expert members shall be appointed subject to consultation between the representatives of the school and those of students, as prescribed by school regulations. <Amended on Sep. 15, 2011; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020>
(4)
 A school may exempt or reduce tuition fees, where the operation of school affairs is not performed normally due to restrictions on the use of school facilities, experiments or practices, or the decrease of school hours, due to disasters defined in subparagraph 1 of 
Article 3 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety
. <Added on Oct. 20, 2020>
(5)
 Schools shall fully reflect the result of deliberation by the enrollment fee deliberation committee unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Added on Sep. 15, 2011; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020>
(6)
 The enrollment fee deliberation committee under paragraph (3) shall set enrollment fees for the corresponding year at a reasonable level, considering grounds based on which the enrollment fees and education expenses per student are calculated under 
Article 6 (1) 8-2 of the Act on Special Cases concerning the Disclosure of Information by Education-Related Institutions
, the average household income for city workers, an annual support plan under 
Article 7-2
 (1), rate of dependence on enrollment fees (referring to the ratio of enrollment fees to total education expenses at a university or college), etc. <Amended on Sep. 15, 2011; Mar. 2, 2016; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020; Mar. 23, 2021; Sep. 24, 2021>
(7)
 The enrollment fee deliberation committee shall discuss the amount subject to exemption from or reduction of enrollment fees under paragraph (4). <Added on Oct. 20, 2020>
(8)
 If necessary for setting enrollment fees, any enrollment fee deliberation committee may request the head of a school to submit relevant data, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the head of a school shall submit relevant data within seven days from the date of receipt of a request unless there is good cause. <Added on Sep. 15, 2011; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020>
(9)
 An enrollment fee deliberation committee shall prepare and keep minutes stating the date, time, place, summary, decisions, etc. of the meeting, and publish them on the website of the school within 10 days from the date of the meeting, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, for at least three years from the date of publication; provided, with respect to matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as matters deemed likely to seriously infringe on the privacy of individuals, the enrollment fee tuition fee deliberation committee may choose not to disclose all or part of the minutes by a resolution of at least 2/3 of the fixed number of its members. <Added on Sep. 15, 2011; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020; Feb. 13, 2024>
(10)
 No school shall set the rate of increase in enrollment fees at a level exceeding 1.5 times the average consumer price inflation for the three immediately preceding years. <Amended on Sep. 15, 2011; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020>
(11)
 Where any school increases the rate of increase in its enrollment fees by more than 1.5 times the average consumer price inflation for the three immediately preceding years notwithstanding paragraph (10), the Minister of Education may impose disadvantages, such as administrative or financial sanctions, etc. on the relevant school. <Amended on Sep. 15, 2011; Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020>
(12)
 Necessary matters such as collection of enrollment fees under paragraph (1), establishment and operation of enrollment fee deliberation committees under paragraph (3), the methods of calculating the rate of increase in enrollment fees under paragraph (10), and administrative and financial sanctions under paragraph (11) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Sep. 15, 2011; Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 3, 2019; Oct. 20, 2020>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 11-2 (Evaluation)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Schools shall conduct a self-inspection and evaluation on education and research, organization and operation, facilities and equipment, etc., as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education, and publicly announce the findings thereof. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(2)
 An institution recognized by the Minister of Education (hereafter in this Article referred to as "recognized institution") may, at the request of a university or college, evaluate or accredit the overall management of a university or college and operation of curricula (including colleges, departments and majors). 
Provided
, That a school having the curricula falling under medicine, dentistry, Korean medicine or nursing shall obtain an evaluation and accreditation from a recognized institution as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 22, 2015>
(3)
 The Minister of Education may designate a relevant specialized evaluation institution, a school consultative body under 
Article 10
, and an organization or a group, etc. designed for the promotion of academic research as an accredited institution. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(4)
 Where the Government intends to provide a university or college with administrative and financial support, it may utilize the outcomes of evaluation or accreditation conducted under paragraph (2).
(5)
 Matters necessary for the evaluation or accreditation under paragraph (2), designation of a recognized institution under paragraph (3) and utilization of the outcomes of evaluation or accreditation under paragraph (4) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 11-3 (Educational statistics surveys)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Minister of Education shall conduct an educational statistics survey every year to collect the basic data on students, teachers, administrative personnel, schools, educational administration agencies, etc. necessary to efficiently implement policies on higher education and research higher education, and shall make public the result of such a survey.
(2)
 The Minister of Education may request the heads of higher education institutions to submit data for the purpose of conducting an educational statistics survey referred to in paragraph (1) (hereafter in this Article referred to as "educational statistics survey"). In such cases, the heads of higher education institutions shall comply with such request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
(3)
 The Minister of Education may request the heads of central administrative agencies, the superintendents of education, and the heads of the institutions concerned, including public institutions under the 
Act on the Management of Public Institutions
, who have related data, to link their data with the others’ data so as to enhance the accuracy of an educational statistics survey and reduce survey-related affairs. In such cases, the heads of the institutions so requested shall comply with such request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
(4)
 The Minister of Education may collect personal data containing the resident registration numbers of the following persons when conducting an educational statistics survey, and may provide to or be provided from the institutions requested for linkage pursuant to paragraph (3) for the purpose of the survey, analysis, verification, etc. of statistics:
1.
 Teachers and staff of the schools and educational administrative agencies subject to the survey;
2.
 Students and graduates of the schools subject to the survey.
(5)
 The Minister of Education may provide the data collected through an educational statistics survey to persons who intend to use such data. In such cases, such data shall be provided in a form in which a specific individual, corporation or organization is unidentifiable, excluding data related to the items disclosed pursuant to the 
Act on Special Cases concerning the Disclosure of Information by Education-Related Institutions
.
(6)
 For efficient formulation, implementation and evaluation of polices on higher education, the Minister of Education may create the indexes, estimated statistics, etc. related to education by utilizing the data collected through an educational statistics survey.
(7)
 For conducting affairs for educational statistics surveys, the Minister of Education may designate a center for national educational statistics and entrust it with such affairs, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the Minister of Education may subsidize expenses necessary for such designation and entrustment.
(8)
 Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (7), matters necessary for objects, procedures, disclosure of result, etc. of educational statistics surveys shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[This Article added on Mar. 21, 2017]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER II STUDENTS AND SCHOOL PERSONNEL

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
SECTION 1 Students

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 12 (Autonomous activities of students)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The self-governing activities of students shall be encouraged and protected, and basic matters concerning the organization and operation thereof shall be determined by school regulations.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 13 (Discipline of students)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The head of a school may discipline any student, if deemed necessary for education, as determined by statutes, regulations, and school regulations. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2021>
(2)
 If the head of a school intends to discipline any student, he or she shall undergo due formalities, such as providing the relevant student with an opportunity to state his or her opinion.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
SECTION 2 School Personnel

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 14 (Classification of school personnel)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Each school (excluding various kinds of schools; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply) shall have the president or dean as the head of a school.
(2)
 School teachers to be assigned to schools shall be classified as professors, associate professors, and assistant professors in addition to presidents and deans referred to in paragraph (1). <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012>
(3)
 Schools shall have personnel such as administrative personnel, etc. necessary for the operation of schools and assistant instructors.
(4)
 Various kinds of schools shall have the required school teachers, personnel and assistant instructors (hereinafter referred to as "faculty"), as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3).
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 14-2 (Instructors)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Instructors referred to in 
Article 14
 (2) shall be appointed by means of a written contract, fixing working conditions including matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the period of employment and wage in compliance with the employment standards and procedures and teaching time prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the term of appointment shall be at least one year; provided, the term of appointment may be less than one year in any of the following cases: <Amended on Mar. 2, 2016; Dec. 18, 2018>
1.
 Where it is necessary for efficiently operating the curricula and classes as an instructor of a distant college (excluding cyber colleges);
2.
 Where an alternative instructor is urgently needed for the remaining period of a semester due to sick leave, maternity leave, taking time off, dispatch, disciplinary action and research year (not more than six months) of teachers for less than six months, or removal from a position, resignation and dismissal of teachers, which occur during the semester.
(2)
 No instructors shall be deemed faculty, in cases of applying the 
Public Educational Officials Act
, the 
Private School Act
 and the 
Pension for Private School Teachers and Staff Act
; provided, the following provisions shall respectively apply 
mutatis mutandis
 to the appointment, guarantee of status, etc. of instructors at any national, public or private school: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Dec. 18, 2018>
1.
 The following provisions to instructors at any national or public school:
(a)

Articles 5
 (1), 10, the main clause of 
Article 10-3
 (1), 11-4 (7), 23, 23-2, 25 (2), 26, 43, the proviso of 
Article 47 (1) and 48 of the Public Educational Officials Act
. In such cases, "dismissal or discharge" in the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of 
Article 10-3 (1) of the Public Educational Officials Act
 shall be construed as "dismissal", "in cases of recommending the appointment of a public educational official under paragraph (1)" in the main clause of 
Article 25 (2) of the said Act
 as "in cases of appointing an instructor", "teaching assistant" in 
Article 26 (1) of the said Act
 as "instructor", and "disciplinary action" in 
Article 43 (2) of the said Act
 as "grounds stipulated in the contract of appointment", respectively;
(b)

Article 33
 and subparagraph 1 of 
Article 69 of the State Public Officials Act
.
2.
 The following provisions to instructors at any private school:
(a)

Articles 23 (2) and (3), 53-2 (1), (2) and (9), 53-4 (1), 54, the main clause of 54-3 (6), 56 and 60 of the Private School Act
. In such cases, "dismissal or discharge" in the main clause of 
Article 54-3 (6) of the Private School Act
 shall be construed as "dismissal", and "disciplinary action" in the main clause of 
Article 56
 (1) of that Act as "grounds stipulated in the contract of appointment", respectively;
(b)

Article 33
 and subparagraph 1 of 
Article 69 of the State Public Officials Act
.
(3)
 Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), procedures for appointing and re-appointing instructors (procedures for reappointment including new appointment shall be guaranteed until the third year, and thereafter, procedures for new appointment, re-appointment, etc. shall be taken) and other necessary matters shall be stipulated by school regulations or articles of incorporation of school foundations in compliance with the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Dec. 18, 2018>
(4)
 Every instructor shall be paid even during the vacation. In such cases, details such as the level of wages shall be prescribed by an appointment contract. <Added on Dec. 18, 2018>
(5)
 The 
Special Act on the Improvement of Teachers’ Status
 and the Protection of Their Educational Activities shall apply to instructors. <Added on Dec. 18, 2018>
[This Article added on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 15 (Functions of school personnel)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The president or dean shall exercise overall control of school affairs, supervise subordinate faculty and guide students.
(2)
 School teachers shall educate and guide students, and do academic research: Provided, if deemed necessary, they may assume full charge of education and guidance, academic research, or industry-academic cooperation pursuant to subparagraph 6 of 
Article 2
 of the Promotion of Industrial Education and Industry-Academic Cooperation Act, as determined by school regulations or the articles of incorporation. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2016>
(3)
 Personnel, including administrative personnel, etc. shall take charge of administrative affairs and other affairs of schools.
(4)
 Assistant instructors shall assist in affairs concerning education, research and school affairs.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 16 (Qualification standards for school teachers and assistant Instructors)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Qualification standards for persons eligible for school teachers or assistant instructors and matters concerning the recognition of their qualifications shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 17 (Part-time teachers)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Every school may have honorary professors, part-time teachers, visiting teachers, etc. in addition to teachers prescribed in 
Article 14
 (2) to have them take charge of education or research, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012; Dec. 18, 2018>
(2)

Article 14-2
 (1) and (2) (excluding 
Article 11-4 (7) of the Educational Officials Act
 and 
Article 53-2 (9) of the Private School Act
) shall apply 
mutatis mutandis
 to part-time teachers, visiting teachers, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "part-time teacher, etc."). In such cases, "instructor" shall be considered as "part-time teacher, etc." <Added on Dec. 18, 2018>
(3)
 Notwithstanding paragraph (2), an employment period of part-time teachers may be less than one year in any of the following cases: <Added on Dec. 18, 2018; Mar. 23, 2021>
1.
 Appointing part-time teachers, etc. to participate in research or industry-academic collaboration lasting less than one year the order of which is placed by institutions other than schools;
2.
 Appointing persons working for the State or local governments (excluding national and public schools prescribed in 
Article 3)
 and public institutions prescribed in 
Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions
 on a regular basis as part-time teachers, etc. for the efficient operation of curricula or classes.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER III SCHOOLS

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
SECTION 1 Common Provisions

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 18 (Names of schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Names of national schools shall be determined by Presidential Decree, those of public schools by ordinance of the relevant local government, and those of private schools by the articles of incorporation of the relevant school foundation.
(2)
 In determining names of schools pursuant to paragraph (1), the term "college" or "university" may be used differently from the kinds of schools referred to in 
Article 2
.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 19 (Organization of schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Schools shall have necessary structures to achieve the purpose of establishment within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2)
 Basic matters concerning the structure of schools shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree and school regulations in cases of national schools, by ordinance of the relevant local government and school regulations in cases of public schools, and by the articles of incorporation of the relevant school foundation and school regulations in cases of private schools.

 Article 60 (Corrective or modification order)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 If any school violates any education-related statute or regulations or order or school regulations thereon in connection with facilities, equipment, classes, school affairs and other matters, the Minister of Education may order the founder, manager or the head of the school to make corrections or modifications within a fixed period. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(2)
 If any person who has received a corrective order or modification order under paragraph (1) fails to comply therewith within a designated period without good cause, the Minister of Education may cancel or suspend the offenses or take such measures as reducing the maximum number of students allowed to enroll in the relevant school, abolishing departments or suspending recruitment of students at the relevant school, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(3)
 Where it is obvious that the violation is not able be corrected or modified based on the nature of such act, such as cases in which violation has already been made, the Minister of Education may take measures pursuant to paragraph (2) without issuing corrective order or modification order pursuant to paragraph (1). <Added on Aug. 13, 2013>

 Article 61 (Order to temporarily or permanently close schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Where it is deemed impossible to hold classes as usual because of urgent circumstances such as a disaster, the Minister of Education may order the head of the relevant school to suspend classes. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(2)
 The head of a school upon receipt of an order referred to in paragraph (1) shall suspend classes without delay.
(3)
 Where the head of a school fails to suspend classes, notwithstanding the order issued under paragraph (1), or where there exists special reasons, the Minister of Education may issue an order to close the school. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
(4)
 For schools that are temporarily closed pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2), classes and student attendance shall be suspended during the suspension period, and for schools closed pursuant to paragraph (3), all functions of the schools, except simple management affairs, shall be suspended.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

 Article 62 (Closure of schools)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Where it is deemed impossible to manage school affairs as usual in one of the following situations, the Minister of Education may order the relevant school foundation to close the school: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 29, 2016>
1.
 Where the head, founder or manager of a school violates this Act or any order issued under this Act by intention or gross negligence;
2.
 Where the head, founder or manager of a school violates more than three times this Act or any order issued by the Minister of Education under other education-related Act and subordinate statutes;
3.
 Where a professional law school suspends classes continuously for three months or more, excluding breaks and holidays.
(2)
 The Minister of Education may order any person that uses the title of a school or recruits students and essentially operates the facility the same way as he or she operates a school, without obtaining authorization to establish a school under 
Article 4
 (2) or a branch school under 
Article 24
, to close such facilities. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
